newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 30.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.

- The Irish Department of Agriculture's special investigation team carried out its first raids on farms on Tuesday where it suspected the BSE disease was deliberately introduced to claim state compensation.
- The Irish Environment Protection Agency said there has been a five percent increase in slight to moderate pollution of Irish rivers over recent years.

- Irish-based pharmaceutical firm Elan formed a new company, Axogen, on Tuesday to sub-contract some of its research and development activities. The new company will be funded by a $90 million public share issue.
- Employees at Irish financial services company Irish Life have been asked to change their working hours to serve customers from 0800 GMT to 2000 GMT.
- Irish airline officials meet on Wednesday to consider taking possible "concerted action" to counter a recent ten percent rise in fuel costs, an Irish air transport body said.
- The Irish government will propose no change in the top rate of income tax over the next three years when talks on a new Irish national wage deal are hammered out over the next few days.
- Palestinian president Yassar Arafat, on a official visit to Ireland on Tuesday, stepped up appeals for continued EU support for his position in the Middle East peace process.
- Irish academic Seamus Deane was pipped at the post for the 20,000 sterling Booker literary prize on Tuesday night when Graham Swift took the award for his book Last Orders.
- Thousands of Irish people are expected to buy Irish Lotto tickets on Wednesday for the record jackpot prize of over six million Irish pounds.
- Irish paper and packaging firm Jefferson Smurfit declined to confirm or deny reports on Tuesday that it was interested in buying South African packaging business Kohler.
- New measures are need to decide which countries and regions are eligible for EU aid, a conference on Irish and European Regional Policy was told on Tuesday.
